15953-the-city-of-delight-a-love-drama-o:
A love drama of the siege and fall of Jerusalem by Elizabeth Miller, author of The Yoke and Saul of Tarsus. The Bobbs-Merrill Company issued it in Indianapolis in 1908, with pictures by F. X. Leyendecker. Miller dedicates the book to her elder brother Otto Miller. A prince's bride opens the tale on the road to Jerusalem.

The shepherd of Pella, travellers by the wayside, and dawn in the hills lead toward imperial Caesar and the young Titus. Greek and Jew meet, and a divine tragedy unfolds as the city falls. Love survives amid siege, fire, and ruin. Miller writes with warmth for ancient faith and feeling, making a famous disaster human in scale.
36421-by-veldt-and-kopje:
By Veldt and Kopje is a book of South African verse and prose by William Charles Scully. This form is dated nineteen seven. The book is writ to a chief of the host. A verse from the old book on the worth of a wise rebuke stands past its name. A long first voice poem lets the lands of Africa speak in turn.

Africa speaks first, as a sphinx whose riddle the realms strive to guess. Greece, Rome, and Persia each smiled on her for a day and were torn for her sport, she says. The great waste speaks of ghost towns and bare bones of men. The Nile land tells how its great god cleft the waste and woke it to life. Town past town of the old north shore takes its turn in the roll.
britannica-1911-backergunje:
Backergunje, or Bakarganj, is a district of British India. It lies in the Dacca division of Eastern Bengal and Assam. It forms part of the joint delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra. Its area runs over 4,542 square miles. No hill rises anywhere in it; flat green country, cut by a network of dark, sluggish streams, meets the eye instead.

Travel goes by boat at every season, since every hollow holds water and land and stream blur together. Villages hide in bamboo and betel-nut groves, the north-west is marsh and rice land, and the southern coast carries the Sundarbans forests, home of tigers and leopards. Great rivers, the Meghna, Arial Khan, and Haringhata, thread the district toward the Bay of Bengal, the Meghna swelling into a wide islanded estuary.
britannica-1911-trebinje:
Trebinje is a place article in the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica about a small town in Herzegovina near the borders of Dalmatia and Montenegro. The town sits nine miles north east of Ragusa on the small river Trebinjcica. About 1,700 people lived there in 1895. It is built in a low, watered hollow among bare limestone hills, and its half ruined wall and citadel speak of a past when its site held real weight in war.

The Slavs built Trebinje, most likely on the site of a Roman town laid waste by the Saracens in 840. Constantine Porphyrogenitus names it Terbunia in the tenth century. The town guarded the road from Ragusa to Constantinople, crossed in 1096 by Raymond of Toulouse and his crusaders. As Tribunia or Travunja it formed part of the Servian Empire until 1355. In 1483 it was taken by the Turks.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-mostar-and-ma:
Mostar and Markana-Trebinje are dioceses in Herzegovina, formed when the Berlin Congress of 1878 let Austria-Hungary occupy Bosnia and Herzegovina. The religious settlement followed at once. In 1881 Emperor Francis Joseph created the church province of Sarajevo, with Banjaluka, Mostar and Markana-Trebinje as suffragans. The Bishop of Mostar administers Markana-Trebinje through a pro-vicar.

Mostar, capital of Herzegovina with 15,000 people including 3,500 Catholics, takes its region's name from the title Herzog, duke, given in 1448 to Grand Waywode Stephan Vukcic. Herzegovina fell to the Turks in 1483 after its last Bosnian king was beheaded in defiance of a promise. The entry traces its peoples, Orthodox, Muslim, Catholic and Jewish, the Eastern Schism, the Bogomil sect, and the church's modern recovery.
doe-osti-3018098-summary-of-yuliang-zhan: Yuliang Zhang's hosted record, LLNL-TR-2015821 from February 2026, written with Ted Laurence, is a short tabular summary of one Lawrence Livermore researcher's roles in funded projects, not a research report. Rows list award dates from 2019 to 2024, funding sources in the laboratory's internal LDRD programs, Zhang's role as principal investigator or co-investigator, project titles, and award totals. Entries include a 500,000 dollar project imaging chromosome protein complexes by high-speed atomic force microscopy, an 8.1 million dollar corrosion project, and two 1.5 million dollar imaging and virtual synapse projects.
doe-osti-3359958-high-penetration-solar-:
Ingemar Mathiasson reports final results for the Northwest Arctic Borough under award DE-IE0000146, dated September 30, 2025, on solar power for Noatak, Alaska. Total costs were about 2.9 million dollars, with a federal share near 2.0 million. The borough and the Native Village of Noatak formed a tribal energy group to run the build. Diesel flown and barged in at high cost has long powered the village, so local solar plus storage promises real savings.

The finished system pairs a solar array with a 495 kilowatt-hour battery and a switchgear controller tied to the diesel plant. The borough set up an independent power producer to sell energy to the Alaska Village Electric Cooperative, with meter checks and billing handled monthly. New workforce roles keep the plant running after the builders leave.
doe-osti-3377896-e2c-cohorts-implementat:
Shannon Anderson, Lauren Reichelt, and Lis Blanco summarize the funded projects of the E2C cohorts in a February 2026 impact deck from the National Laboratory of the Rockies. E2C offers three depths of technical assistance. In-depth partnerships run about three years and support nine communities now. Peer-learning cohorts run about six months and reach about 100 communities per year. Expert Match gives three to six months of no-cost help to about 200 communities per year.

Case summaries show what the money did. One Clean Cities cohort helped Vancouver build transportation electrification training and a train-the-trainer model, co-hosting 12 community engagement events that drew input from 403 people for the city's 2025 plan. Another paired Drive Clean Colorado with Fort Collins Utilities on an e-mobility needs assessment built with a community advisory group.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DucoteJeromeSch: A news article reports admissions made by Jerome Ducote in connection with an investigation involving farm labor leader Cesar Chavez. The names Schering and Henry are also attached to the archived file. The surviving record gives the article's subject but no paper, date, or detail of what Ducote admitted, so it stands as a brief news report tied to the Chavez investigation.
nasa-tm-19670013511-effect-of-simulated-:
Roy G. Stabe, John F. Kline, and Edward H. Gibbs, of NASA's Lewis Research Center in Cleveland, tested a rocket turbine question in this study. Turbopump drive turbines power the pumps that feed rocket engines. Their bearings need cooling, and coolant leaking into the flow could change how the turbine performs.

The team ran experiments at Lewis on a scale model turbine. They fed measured amounts of extra air ahead of the first rotor to simulate bearing coolant. At design speed and pressure ratio, added secondary flow lowered the turbine's work output and efficiency. Each added increment also raised the pressures between stages, most sharply at the nozzle exit.
podcast-joerogan-caK7O-T6rJE:
Writer Sebastian Junger tells Rogan, in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, about his brush with death. Junger, author of Tribe and The Perfect Storm, suffered a sudden internal bleed at home and nearly died before help arrived. He later wrote about what he saw as he faded.

He describes the presence he felt beside him, which he, an unbeliever, could not explain away. Rogan asks what the hour changed in his thinking about death and his father's ghost. The segment is a war reporter's most personal story, told with the same plain care he gave to soldiers' tales.
podcast-joerogan-eEOXc9ufQjE:
Rick Doblin talks MDMA with Rogan in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, busting myths and detailing breakthroughs. Doblin founded MAPS to turn MDMA into a legal therapy for trauma. By this visit, his trials had reached their final, decisive stage.

He separates the drug's real risks from the scare stories of the drug-war years, and lays out what the trial data showed for PTSD patients. Rogan asks what legal treatment would look like in practice. The segment is an advocate's update at a hopeful moment, careful with the facts because the finish line was finally in sight.
the-city-of-delight-a-love-drama-of-the-: Elizabeth Miller, author of The Yoke and Saul of Tarsus, wrote this love drama of the siege and fall of Jerusalem, published at Indianapolis by the Bobbs-Merrill Company in March 1908. Only the title page, dedication, and the start of the contents are present here. The chapters open with A Prince's Bride and On the Road to Jerusalem. Later titles name the Shepherd of Pella, Imperial Caesar, and the Young Titus.The front matter is all a reader gets in this record.
